subject: Vector fit scouting + pilot request — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@searchlytics.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vector fit scouting + pilot request — next steps

Hi Laura / Marcus —

Thanks again for taking time today. Short recap from our discovery and clear next steps so we stay aligned. I captured a few concrete asks below.

What we heard (short):
- Use case: semantic search + "did-you-mean" suggestions across ~25M docs, mixed content (KB articles, product descriptions, short support tickets).
- Latency target: 50–120ms p50 for single-vector retrieval in US West.
- Success metrics: retrieval Recall@10 and MRR are primary; also monitor false-positive rate on fuzzy matches.
- Drift concern: content updates weekly with a ~10% churn of items; they want a simple drift alerting approach.

Our proposed immediate plan:
1) Pilot evaluation (2 weeks) — we run a scoped embedding fit using their 10k sample (they can expand to 50k if pilot looks good). Benchmarks we will produce: Recall@1/5/10, MRR, average cosine distance distributions, and embedding dimensionality sensitivity (64/128/256/768).
2) Model candidates — starting recommendations: a dense open model tuned for semantic retrieval (open-embed-large-384), plus a higher-dim family (text-embed-768-like) for recall-sensitive slices. We will also surface a quantized variant for latency/cost tradeoffs.
3) Prompt set & evaluation artifacts — attaching a starter prompt_set_v1.csv (search intents + labels) and a short evaluation harness link.
4) Drift monitoring — propose weekly cohort sampling + a simple KL/divergence signal on embedding norm/density + monthly reindex cadence.

Ask of you (Laura / Marcus):
- Send the 10k sample (anonymized) and a short list of gold queries you care about (5–10).
- Confirm whether embedding dimensionality budget has a hard cap (e.g., must be <=256) due to existing vector index constraints.

If you’re good with the pilot outline we can start Thurs Jun 21. Ben will spin up the evaluation harness and Grace will be the CS lead for onboarding.

Thanks —
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@searchlytics.io>

Cc: Marcus Holt <marcus.holt@searchlytics.io>
Date: Wed, 20 Jun 2028 10:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vector fit scouting + pilot request — next steps

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear summary — this matches our internal read. A couple of clarifications:  

- Latency: our production stack currently targets p50 < 120ms and p95 < 350ms; if you can show a path to p95 <= 350ms we're comfortable.
- Dimensionality: we don't have a hard cap, but storage is a consideration; prefer <= 512 if quality/latency tradeoffs are similar.
- Drift: weekly sampling + simple alerting is fine; we also want an approach that flags when a new document type (e.g., long-form tutorial) starts to appear frequently.

I attached a 10k sample (search_sample.csv) and included 7 gold queries with expected matches in the file.

We can confirm the pilot start on Thu Jun 21 — please go ahead and schedule kickoff. Also, please add any required NDA/PSA paperwork; procurement may want a short statement of data handling.

Best,
Laura

Attachment: search_sample.csv (CSV, 2.1MB)

Subject: Fwd: Vector fit scouting + pilot request — next steps

Ben / Grace — forwarding Laura's sample and confirmation. Notes for prioritization and quick triage: 

- Priority: pilot start Thu 2028-06-21 (today). Ben, please provision the eval harness and run baseline embeddings for open-embed-large-384 + high-dim candidate (we'll call it text-embed-768 for shorthand).
- Benchmarks to capture (minimum): Recall@1/5/10, MRR, average inference latency (p50/p95), mean cosine distributions, percent of queries that changed top-1 when switching dimensionality.
- Acceptance threshold proposal (for pilot handoff): Recall@10 >= 0.75 OR MRR >= 0.45 on the 10k sample. If neither is met, we surface qualitative failure modes and recommend next steps (prompt engineering, model variant, or reindex strategy).
- Drift guardrails: compute weekly embedding centroid shift and a simple outlier rate (top-100 nearest neighbor overlap drop). If centroid shift > 0.12 (cosine) or overlap drop > 0.2, trigger CS review.

Grace — can you own the procurement/PSA check and let me know if we need a short data processing addendum? I'll handle the technical run and benchmarks.

Thanks —
Marissa
